title: A tiny scalar autograd engine
hints: Every operation builds a new Value that remembers its inputs (_prev) and a closure _backward that, given the output's grad, adds the local derivative times out.grad onto each input's grad. For a * b: a.grad += b.data * out.grad and b.grad += a.data * out.grad.
Accumulate with += rather than =. A variable used twice (a * a + a) receives a gradient from each use and the total is their sum. That is also why the caller must zero grads between backward passes.

backward(): build a topological order of the graph by depth-first search from the root (append a node after visiting all its children), set root.grad = 1, then call node._backward() for every node in reverse order. Each node's grad is complete before its own _backward runs.
